Serve a ball into the board. It hops left or right off one post in each of 12 rows and lands in one of 13 courts, which pays its multiplier times your stake.

Eight-deck Punto Banco, shuffled for every coup. Back the hand that ends closer to 9.

Player pays 1 to 1. Banker pays 1 to 1 less 5% commission: 19 for every 20. Tie pays 8 to 1, and Player and Banker bets push on a tie. Pairs pay 11 to 1.

Aces count 1, tens and courts 0. Third cards follow the fixed tableau.

Send a pizza into the wood-fired oven. The longer it bakes the more it is worth: pulling it out pays your stake times the multiplier on the oven gauge.

It can burn at any moment, and a burnt pizza pays nothing. Where it burns is drawn before the dough touches the stone, so nothing you do changes it — only when you choose to pull it out.

Set the oven timer before the bake and it comes out at exactly that multiplier, whatever the frame rate. Every timer setting returns the same 97%%, so bake as long as your nerve allows.
